cells.action: Implement contract decision a653682b (D1 4bf3a432, D2 f613e3c2) in a new module verbs/cells/rigor_floor.rs. Rows are {glob, min_lane, flags, owner_first}. Built-in rows (schema-shaped, not every SQL file): `**/migrations/**`, `**/migrate/**`, `**/alembic/versions/**`, `**/schema.sql`, `**/*.schema.sql` and `**/schema.prisma` at min_lane high-risk, flags [data-model], owner_first true; `.github/workflows/release*` and `.github/workflows/publish*` at min_lane standard, no flags, owner_first true. Repo rows come from the `.bee/config.json` key `rigor_floor` (an array of the same shape), read through read_config_raw (state.rs `pub fn read_config_raw(root: &Path) -> Map<String, Value> {`); a malformed row is skipped with a warning on stderr. For a file, the effective floor is the highest min_lane, the union of flags and the OR of owner_first over every matching row, built-in and repo alike, so a repo row can raise and never lower. Lane rank: docs < tiny < small < standard < high-risk, spike ranks as standard (workflows.rs triage_ladder_rank covers only three lanes; do not change it). Flag names must be in the route flag vocabulary in workflows.rs. Use the write guard's glob matcher: `crate::hooks::write_guard::{glob_tokens, glob_match}` (the paths module is private but re-exported by write_guard/mod.rs; design_group.rs already imports it this way); glob_match takes `&[char]`, so collect the path's chars first as paths.rs does; write_guard/tests.rs already proves `**/migrations/**` against db/migrations/001.sql. No new crate dependency. Register the module in cells/mod.rs with `mod rigor_floor;` plus `pub(crate) use self::rigor_floor::*;`. The lane vocabulary ROUTE_LANE_VALUES in workflows.rs is private, so the rank covers all six lanes itself. Export a lookup that takes the root and a list of files and returns the hits (path, row glob, row source built-in or repo, floor), and an owner-first query. Wire the check: in validate.rs beside `match assert_regen_obligation(map, "addCell") {` (problems are collected there, not thrown) and in handlers_write.rs beside `assert_regen_obligation(&merged, "updateCell")?;` (thrown before write_cell). The add seam covers single and batch add; validate_new_cell_problems has no feature argument, so read map["feature"]; a cell with no feature skips the check. On update, run the lane check first, then the owner-first check below. Read the feature route (lane and flags) the way drivers/close.rs feature_route does: the lane record's route first, then the state.json route when it belongs to the feature (feature_route returns only the lane; read the flags beside it). No recorded route: no check. Refuse with the in-message token RIGOR_FLOOR (the REGEN_OBLIGATION style: `addCell: RIGOR_FLOOR — ...`; refusals carry no code field) when a hit's min_lane ranks above the route lane or a hit flag is missing from the route flags; the message names the path, the row glob, whether the row is built-in or from .bee/config.json, the floor, that an owner-first row also needs a human gate, and the remedy: `bee route --set --class <class> --lane <floor lane> --flags <route flags plus missing> --files <n>`. Owner-first at cells add/update: when a cell file hits an owner-first row and the feature's execution gate (or merged gate) is approved with actor auto in the workflow record (gates.<name>.actor), refuse with GATE_OWNER_FIRST — this closes the path where a route raised after an auto gate lets an owner-first cell in with no human gate. GATE GATE_OWNER_FIRST in set_gate.rs (contract decision 49388de3, D3 f9ba8d88): when actor is auto (`let actor = flag_value(flags, "actor").unwrap_or_else(|| "user".to_string());`) and the call approves shape, execution or --merge, collect the feature's files from the lane record's gate_preview cell packet (`if let Some(prev) = state.get("gate_preview").cloned() {`) and from the feature's persisted cells (list_cells for the feature), ask the owner-first query, and on any hit refuse at every bypass level. Check once before the lock the way the uat refusal does (`if actor == "auto" && name == "uat" {`, reading the record with peek_target_record), and AGAIN against target.record() after acquire_mutation_locks and before the write, because gate_preview can change between the peek and the lock (the preview check already runs twice for this reason). The GATE_OWNER_FIRST message names the path and the row glob and tells the leader: stop; do not retry; do not pass --actor user; run `bee state waiting-on set --kind gate --subject "<feature> owner-first gate"`, show the gate to the human, and end the turn. An approval with actor user, a refusal (approved false), and an auto approval with no owner-first hit are unchanged. Tests red-first: add refuses a small-lane cell on db/migrations/001.sql under a small route; add passes under a high-risk route with data-model; db/migrate, alembic/versions and schema.prisma paths hit; a fixture tests/fixtures/report.sql passes; a repo config row raises a floor; a repo row with a lower lane does not lower a built-in floor; update refuses the same way; a feature with no route is not checked; unmatched paths pass; add of an owner-first cell after an auto-approved execution gate refuses GATE_OWNER_FIRST, and passes after a user-approved gate. Gate tests next to gate_refuses_uat_from_actor_auto_and_writes_nothing: auto merge refused with an owner-first file in the preview packet and nothing written, and the message names waiting-on; the same with actor user approves; auto merge with no owner-first file approves as before.
